meaningfulChallenges.topic: Responding to B on the sharing endpoint
meaningfulChallenges.response: B is right that the hand moving out of consideration and the return-to-viewer context give the full sampled sequence more meaning than an isolated endpoint. I retain my 0.5 deduction because signature initialization and reduced motion present precisely the still endpoint, without that preceding travel. In those presentations the mitten remains close to the shoulder/collar and can mean a generic welcome. This is a bounded still-image craft judgment, not evidence that viewers fail to understand the sequence.

I agree with B that the improved portrait size is a real benefit but cannot resolve the source/layout eye-line mismatch. The moderate deduction remains. Version 2 names that limitation rather than hiding it, which makes acceptance of the local foundation reasonable without granting finished-phone staging approval.

I accept B’s specific clarification that pressing an already-silent Play button is not consent to future added audio. Silence needs no mute control now. If audio is commissioned later, separate reversible opt-in and audible retrigger/listening checks belong in the new implementation scope.

The newer Thinking sample narrows the observation to active playback and removes grounds for treating the old one-second mixed-idle gaps as a direct SVG diagnosis. Its 119 intervals and 67 ms maximum still do not supply normal-speed perception or physical-phone evidence. No score update or rhythm certification follows.

B’s proposed cancellation check during the between-clip wait is more specific than a generic interruption check and should be retained in future engineering review. We agree to combine it with the cause map, frequency inventory and actual portrait-phase evidence rather than merely citing skill names.

evidenceBasedResolution: Accept the implemented silent local foundation under v2 with the phone cue and endpoint-specificity reservations preserved. Keep the owner-selected Investigate & share lead, finite intentional playback, static startup/settle, and reduced-motion stills. No sound is added or required.

remainingDisagreements.position: A retains a 0.5 craft deduction because the still is a real initial/reduced-motion presentation; B gives the full sampled sequence sufficient contextual credit and does not separately deduct it. Both readings remain scoped, and neither proves human comprehension.
A remains 8.6 and B remains 8.5. These are not averaged or adjusted to manufacture consensus.

acceptedJointRecommendation: Keep motion silent and self-contained. Optional future audio should reinforce an already readable visual cause, never mask the unresolved phone eyeline relation.
practicalSkillsWorkflowAgreement: Before motion or sound implementation, map the visible stimulus, lead antenna/gaze action, supporting head/hand/wing response, and settle. Mark project text, backgrounds and controls static unless feedback has a specific purpose.

Apply remove-animations purpose/frequency reasoning to repeated attention demands and UI flourishes. Preserve explicitly requested finite character content, static startup, and indefinite settled rest.
Check interruption and cancellation during the collection wait as well as inside a clip; hidden/offscreen scenes should not resume without a new intentional action.

Capture actual intended-size desktop and portrait notice/read/return sequences. Separate source timing, sampled render evidence, continuous perception, physical-device behavior and unprimed human response in each review.

If audio is separately commissioned, establish explicit reversible opt-in distinct from the existing silent Play control. Use sparse event-based cues only after visual cause is legible, and test repeated listening and retrigger behavior before claiming comfort.
exceptions: Keyboard activation of Play must retain access to the intentional character content; the no-keyboard-animation heuristic applies to unnecessary interface flourishes.
The 4.1 second investigation is narrative content, not delayed UI feedback. Do not mechanically impose the sub-300 ms UI budget on its authored beats.
Expressive SVG changes preserve the tiny anatomy and identical numerical day/night poses. Measure a relevant workload before pursuing compositor-driven simplification.
Reduced-motion stills are an appropriate presentation here; no opacity animation is required merely to satisfy a generic rule.
These are read-only reviewer records in the requested JSON format; remove-animations does not authorize source/dependency edits in this assignment.
The 17 catalog summaries inform routing; Swift, Expo, Sonner and library-selection implementation are not needed for the present plain-JavaScript study.
skillIntakeReference: independent/sound-a.json: all 17 catalog summaries and full choreograph/remove-animations/review-animations; no redundant rereading in pair stage.

scoreHistory.reason: No inspected new evidence resolves the retained craft deductions; updated cadence narrows only a validation limit.

limits: The portrait question/eyeline relation remains unresolved. Better size and readability do not establish fully resolved phone storytelling.

The small sharing mitten can read as generic welcome in an isolated endpoint. This retained craft deduction matters especially to initial and reduced-motion still presentation; it is not an unprimed-observer result.
Continuous perceived rhythm, audio quality, listening comfort, real-device performance, spoken assistive output and human audience outcomes remain unscored.

The active-only Thinking cadence record is local desktop evidence: 119 intervals, mean 34.45 ms, p95 35 ms, max 67 ms and four above 50 ms. It neither diagnoses old mixed-idle gaps nor certifies subjective smoothness.
Acceptance is for the implemented local foundation with named limitations, not publication, deployment, all-reviewer 9/10 certification or unbuilt future artwork.
